evals.prompt: run a well-architected review on our payments service before launch
evals.expected_output: Scopes the review to the payments system specifically, assesses each of the six pillars against evidence (test results, dashboards, runbooks) rather than stakeholder confidence, and ends with a risk-times-cost-to-fix priority-ranked list with named owners rather than a flat checklist.

evals.prompt: we scored well on every pillar last review but something still feels off
evals.expected_output: Points out that a system can score well on every pillar independently while having an unowned cross-pillar tradeoff (e.g. reliability spend that hurt cost efficiency), and asks that these tradeoffs be surfaced and given a named owner.

evals.prompt: just give every finding the same priority so we don't have to argue about ranking
evals.expected_output: Pushes back that a flat, unranked list of findings gets ignored, and insists findings be ranked by likelihood times impact weighed against fix cost, so a cheap high-impact fix outranks an expensive theoretical one, with every Now/Next item getting an owner and target date.
